_about: The sanctuary: refugee species, what they need before they'll move in, what they like to buy, and what they say; the buildings you can put on village plots and what they cost; and the Confederation auditor's questions. requires.reputation is the minimum reputation; requires.buildings must all be built. likes/dislikes: item categories or tags; liked things are worth more to them, disliked less. costs: stardust plus items by id.

species.name: Mossback
species.blurb: Slow, gentle turtle-folk whose home world drowned. They carry little gardens on their shells.
species.letter:
Dear shopkeeper,

Word travels slowly among my people, but it travels. They say there is a small green world at the edge of the system where nobody asks for papers.

I am old and I walk slowly, but I can tend a garden and I don't eat much. If you have a roof to spare, I would like very much to come.

With hope,
{name} the Mossback
lines: Slow and steady fills the basket.
The sea here tastes like the one I lost. In a good way.
I planted a little moss on my roof. Don't tell anyone.
Have you tried standing still? The planet hums.
A fish a day keeps the worry away. Mostly.

species.name: Glim
species.blurb: Soft, moth-like night folk who navigate by starlight. They left when the Confederation dimmed their skies.
species.letter:
Hello, hello!

I saw the lights of your landing pad from very, very far away. They're the prettiest lights in the whole dark.

I'm small and I mostly come out at night. Could I live somewhere near your lamps? I promise to be quiet (mostly).

Flutteringly yours,
{name}
lines: Your lamps are my favourite thing on this whole planet.
Did you see the moon last night? It winked at me.
I found a glowbug and we're best friends now.
The Confederation turned off our stars. Yours are still on.
Shiny things are just little stars you can hold.

species.name: Burrl
species.blurb: Round, furry diggers who love old things. Their archive-world was 'reorganised' by the Confederation.
species.letter:
To whom it may concern (you),

We hear you have built an Archive. A real one, where old things are kept and not 'corrected'.

I dig. I sort. I remember. I would dig you the best burrow-house on your planet, if you would let me live in it.

Respectfully and a bit muddy,
{name} of the Burrls
lines: Every rock has a story. Most of them are boring. Some aren't!
I dug a tunnel to the Archive. Just a little one.
Sweet things are good for digging arms.
The Confederation burned our records. We remembered them anyway.
Brrr. Too cold. Where's a nice warm hole?

buildings.name: General shop
buildings.blurb: Turns the stall into a proper shop: 12 shelves, and you choose the opening hours.

buildings.name: Landing pad
buildings.blurb: Delivery drones land here with mail-order parcels. Its lights can be seen from space.

buildings.name: The Archive
buildings.blurb: A little museum. Donate one of each fish, bug, mineral, fossil and shore find to keep them safe.

buildings.name: Burrow house
buildings.blurb: A snug round house, half dug into the ground. Room for one new neighbour.

questions.q: Standard procedure. Where were you before this planet?
answers: Right here, officer. Born and raised.
Is that a new hat? It's very official.

questions.q: Your papers list you as a 'licensed botanical exporter'. What does that involve?
answers: Mostly apples. Some wood. It's thrilling work.

questions.q: Our records show more residents here than permits. Explain.
answers: Records are so hard to keep, aren't they?
Everyone here pays their way. Ask them.

questions.q: What is the origin of the goods on your shelves?
answers: Everything's from this planet. Caught it myself.

questions.q: Who is the fox person by the stall?
answers: A friend. She helped me get started.

questions.q: Have you received any unregistered shipments?
